newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 14.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Tuesday's edition of The Wall Street Journal:
- American Standard rebuffed the $4 billion takeover bid from Tyco International.
- NationsBank, J.P. Morgan and some other big banks posted better than expected quarterly earnings.
- The FDA proposed withdrawing its approval for allergy drug Seldane over its potential side effects.
- Guess is moving most of its jeans-making south of the border amid allegations of illegal labor practices.
- Nextel is expected to announce that some of its customers can travel to 50 different cities and still pay home rates, a first in the wireless business.
- Intel CEO Andrew Grove will hand over the title of president to Craig Barrett.
- The new technology czar at General Motors wants to put some $500 million worth of work now done by EDS up for grabs.
- Investors are pouring money into stock mutual funds so far this month at a pace far exceeding December's.
- Republic Industries said it secured a formal agreement from GM that will allow it to acquire GM car and truck franchises throughout the U.S.
- Dow Jones shares rose 8.7 percent following a published report about pressure to improve its stock price being exerted by two members of the family that has long controlled the company.
- Former Smith Barney chief Frank Zarb is the leading candidate to become the next head of the NASD.
- Moody's once solid lead in the bond ratings business is shrinking as it faces customer complaints and a Justice Department inquiry.
- American Greetings said it is considering quitting some of its noncore consumer-product businesses.
- EMC is expected to release a new line of disk drive storage products.
- Norfolk Southern vowed to buy almost $1 billion of Conrail shares if it wins a shareholder vote this week.

- Chicago financier Sam Zell, known as a shrewd dealmaker, wants to combine four real estate investment funds he runs into a single public REIT that would likely have a stock market value of more than $2.5 billion.
- Bonds suffered through a lackluster session with few investors willing to place bets ahead of Tuesday's release of new consumer price data.
